statements.proof_tex:
On a compact active-interior allocation set there is \(\rho>0\) with \(C_{C,k}/C\geq\rho/2\) eventually for every \(k\in A\).  Each target cell in stratum \(k\) has conditional probability \(1/M_k\).  A within-stratum pilot tending to infinity and equal to \(o(C_{C,k})\) therefore yields, by bounded Chebyshev inequalities and a finite union bound, uniformly consistent cell moments and \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\).  The remaining stratum shares retain the same positive limits, and quotient covariances lie in a compact uniformly positive-definite set.

Snap the estimate to the rational partition from \(\texttt{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\).  Conditional on labels and the pilot, main observations are independent.  The bounded triangular-array expansion in \(\texttt{prop:efficient-exact-hit-cr-face}\) and the local mean calculation in \(\texttt{thm:target-tangent-lan-cr}\) hold uniformly on the compact allocation and representative sets.  Represented-selector boundaries are Gaussian-null, and the finite receipt family makes conditional risk convergence uniform.  The causal-loss expansion (82) is unchanged, so the displayed upper bound follows; the pilot fraction vanishes because each pilot is \(o(C_{C,k})\).

The slow diagonal construction with tolerance \(1/j\) gives uniform convergence to \(G_{A,M}(v_A,\alpha_A)\).  The conclusion is simultaneous over the finite retained subsets.  If an active share tends to zero, pilot consistency is not uniform and covariance leaves every compact positive-definite cell, so no positive-rate transfer is claimed.  Taking \(A=\mathcal K\) and bounding all shares below gives exactly the stated global-candidate scope.

statements.statement:
For every fixed finite \(K\), the routine \(\mathfrak C_K\) gives an arbitrary-\(\varepsilon\) validated certificate in the following extended-value sense.  Fix a declared face \(A\subseteq\mathcal K\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and a compact rational cell of positive \((v_A,r_A)\) on which \(\Omega_A\) is uniformly positive definite.  A deterministic algorithm enumerates every nonempty retained subset \(S\subseteq A\), invokes the compact certificates at explicitly computed radii, and returns a represented randomized selector and outward-rounded numbers satisfying
\[
L^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)
\leq \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}\right]
\leq U^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A},
\qquad U^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}-L^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}\leq\varepsilon.
\]
It makes the independent Gaussian split explicit: the screening observation has covariance \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/\lambda\), the decision observation has covariance \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/(1-\lambda)\), and the compact selector receives the decision observation multiplied by \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\).  Coordinates within a fixed threshold of the screening maximum are retained.  Hence partial-tie limits such as \((0,-a,-M)\) enter their retained lower-dimensional game rather than an invalid radial truncation.  Uniformity is over retained subsets of this declared face; global adaptation over every candidate policy requires taking \(A=\mathcal K\) with positive information for every candidate.

The same routine certifies both outer designs.  Over \(p\in\Delta_K\), it returns a risk interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\), rational simplex cells containing every minimizer of \(p\mapsto G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)\), and a feasible \(\varepsilon\)-optimal \(p\).  Over \(a\in\Delta_A\), it returns the analogous objects for \(a\mapsto G_A(v_A,a)\).  A zero action-relevant coordinate has the proved extended value \(+\infty\); a computable two-arm lower bound excludes a whole boundary neighborhood before finite interior branch-and-bound.

For primitive implementation, partition the \(C\) clusters into three disjoint prespecified pieces of sizes \(m_C\), \(N_C^{\mathrm s}\), and \(N_C^{\mathrm d}\), where \(m_C\to\infty\), \(m_C/C\to0\), \(N_C^{\mathrm s}/C\to\lambda\), and \(N_C^{\mathrm d}/C\to1-\lambda\).  Form separate calibrated screening and decision estimators.  Their \(\sqrt C\)-limits have covariances \(\Sigma/\lambda\) and \(\Sigma/(1-\lambda)\), respectively, and the compact selector is applied to \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\) times the decision statistic.  With pilot covariance snapping, the asymptotic scaled simple regret is uniformly bounded by the certified Gaussian upper value over the Bernoulli outer simplex and over each compact active-interior exact-count allocation set.  The transfer is simultaneous over the finitely many retained subsets of the declared face and over triangular bounded-schedule arrays whose covariance stays in the certified cells.  Fixed-scale inferior policies have vanishing scaled contribution; \(C^{-1/2}\)-scale policies enter the retained compact game.  For global candidate adaptation take \(A=\mathcal K\); under exact counts this also requires all candidate shares in a compact simplex interior.  At a vanishing action-relevant share only \(+\infty\) is asserted.  A diagonal sequence of tolerances, split fractions, pilot sizes, and certificate meshes transfers the certified noncompact Gaussian value and outer design on exactly these domains.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove Gaussian certification, outer optimization, and normalized primitive transfer in turn.

\emph{Step 1: unbounded Gaussian certification.}
Fix a terminal covariance cell and write \(d=|A|\).  Compactness and uniform positive definiteness give a computable bound \(\bar\sigma\) on all coordinate standard deviations.  The largest-coordinate rule has, for a best arm \(b\) and gaps \(d_i=h_b-h_i\), risk at most
\[
\sum_{i\ne b}d_i\Phi\!\left(-\frac{d_i}{\sqrt{\sigma_i^2+\sigma_b^2}}\right)
\leq\frac{(d-1)\bar\sigma}{\sqrt\pi}=:H_0. \tag{83}
\]
The Mills bound proved in \(\texttt{lem:hierarchical-gaussian-screening}\) gives the inequality.  Choose rational \(0<\lambda<1\) and rational \(T>0\) so that, for \(a_\lambda=\sqrt{2/\lambda}\bar\sigma\),
\[
\{(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}-1\}H_0\leq\varepsilon/4,\qquad
\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}\leq\varepsilon/4. \tag{84}
\]
These searches terminate as \(\lambda\downarrow0\) and \(T\to\infty\), and directed rational arithmetic certifies them.  For every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\), choose rational
\[
M_S\geq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,T\sqrt{|S|-1}. \tag{85}
\]
Use the exact zero value for a singleton; otherwise invoke \(\texttt{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\) with error \(\eta\) satisfying \((1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\eta\leq\varepsilon/4\), obtaining \(L_S\leq G_{S,M_S}\leq U_S\) and \(U_S-L_S\leq\eta\).  Define
\[
L^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq A}L_S,\qquad
U^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\max_SU_S
+\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}. \tag{86}
\]
The screening lemma gives the lower and selector upper inequalities.  If \(S_\star\) maximizes \(U_S\), then
\[
\max_SU_S\leq L_{S_\star}+\eta\leq\max_SL_S+\eta.
\]
Together with \(\max_SL_S\leq G_A\leq H_0\), (84)--(86) imply \(U^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}-L^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}<\varepsilon\).  There are only \(2^d-1\) subsets, and the receipt records all split, radius, compact-certificate, tail, and rounding data.  No radial restriction on \(h\) is used.

\emph{Step 2: outer-simplex certification.}
For Bernoulli labels,
\[
(Bp)_k\geq\underline q_k:=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}>0
\quad(p\in\Delta_K,k\in A). \tag{87}
\]
Partition the explicit constraints \(p_\ell\geq0\), \(\sum_\ell p_\ell=1\) into rational simplex cells.  Linear interval evaluation gives \(q^-\leq Bp\leq q^+\).  By \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-information-order}\), evaluation at \(q^+\) is a cell lower bound, while a feasible rational point supplies an upper incumbent.  If relative coordinate width is at most \(\xi<1\), the unresolved multiplicative variation is bounded by \((1-\xi)^{-1/2}-(1+\xi)^{-1/2}\), which tends uniformly to zero under refinement because of (87).  Branch-and-bound therefore terminates with a width-\(\varepsilon\) value interval, all surviving optimizer cells, and an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal feasible \(p\).

For exact counts, optimize under
\[
a_i\geq0\ (i\in A),\qquad\sum_{i\in A}a_i=1. \tag{88}
\]
A zero active rate has value \(+\infty\) by the information-order lemma.  For positive rates, the subface lower bound and \(\texttt{thm:two-policy-minimax}\) give, for distinct \(i,j\),
\[
G_A(v_A,a)\geq\kappa\sqrt{v_i/a_i+v_j/a_j}\geq\kappa\sqrt{v_i/a_i}. \tag{89}
\]
Let \(\underline v>0\) be the cellwise lower bound and \(\overline U\) a certified finite upper bound at the uniform allocation.  Choose rational
\[
0<\eta_0<\min\left\{\frac1{2d},\frac{\kappa^2\underline v}{4(\overline U+1)^2}\right\}. \tag{90}
\]
If \(a_i<\eta_0\), (89) exceeds \(\overline U\); thus every minimizer lies in the compact polytope (88) with \(a_i\geq\eta_0\).  The positive-cell branch-and-bound above terminates there.  This proves both outer computations without evaluating a positive-rate formula at zero.

\emph{Step 3: normalized primitive transfer.}
Use disjoint prespecified pilot, screening, and decision cluster sets with
\[
m_C+N_C^{\mathrm s}+N_C^{\mathrm d}=C,\quad
m_C\to\infty,\quad m_C/C\to0,\quad
N_C^{\mathrm s}/C\to\lambda,\quad
N_C^{\mathrm d}/C\to1-\lambda. \tag{91}
\]
Under complete randomization, split separately within every active stratum.  The randomization and schedule-independence assumptions give independence of the three outcome arrays conditional on prespecified counts.

Let \(\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm s}\) and \(\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm d}\) be the calibrated estimators formed from the corresponding pieces.  In the Bernoulli regime, every used cell satisfies
\[
\rho_z=q_k/M_k\geq\min_\ell B_{k\ell}/M_k>0,\qquad z\in\mathcal S_k, \tag{92}
\]
while in the certified exact-count interior its limiting frequency is at least \(\eta_0/M_k\).  Expanding each cell ratio, uniformly because the reciprocals in (92) are bounded, gives for \(b\in\{\mathrm s,\mathrm d\}\)
\[
\widetilde U_{C,k}^{b}-U_k
=\frac1{N_C^b}\sum_{c\in b}\frac{\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}}{q_k}
\{W_c(Z_c)-\mu_{Z_c}\}+o_P((N_C^b)^{-1/2}), \tag{93}
\]
with \(q_k\) replaced by the active exact-count share in that regime.  Bounded characteristic-function expansions, equivalently the corresponding compact oracle-transfer results, yield jointly
\[
\sqrt C(\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm s}-U)\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma/\lambda),\qquad
\sqrt C(\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm d}-U)\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma/(1-\lambda)), \tag{94}
\]
with independent limits.  The screen uses contrasts of the first statistic, and the compact rule receives
\[
\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,\sqrt C\,\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm d}. \tag{95}
\]
Translation invariance removes the common location.  Under local displacement \(h\), (95) has contrast mean \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}h\) and covariance \(\Sigma\), exactly matching the Gaussian screening construction and its \((1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\) regret rescaling.  Thus both split covariances and the decision normalization are explicit.

Pilot empirical moments are uniformly consistent by boundedness and (92), so outward covariance snapping selects a certified cell or recorded neighbor with probability tending to one.  A binomial lower-tail bound and Hoeffding's inequality conditional on assignments give uniform constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) such that
\[
\Pr\{\sqrt C|\widetilde U_{C,k}^{\mathrm s}-U_k|>x\}
\leq c_1e^{-c_2x^2}+c_1e^{-c_2C},\qquad0\leq x\leq\sqrt C. \tag{96}
\]
The screening lemma's pairwise decomposition then gives a deterministic \(b(T)\downarrow0\) bounding the scaled regret from deleting a best arm or retaining a set with scaled range above \(2T\), up to \(o(1)\).  In particular, coordinates with diverging scaled gaps contribute \(o(1)\).

For uniformity, suppose a violating triangular sequence existed.  The bounded schedule space is compact metric, so \(\texttt{lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws}\) gives a subsequence of schedule laws converging weakly.  Bounded continuous coordinate welfares and their squares make all means and variances converge; pass again so every nonnegative scaled gap converges in \([0,\infty]\).  Infinite-gap coordinates vanish from regret by (96).  On the remaining finite-gap coordinates, (93)--(95) give joint pilot-screen-decision Gaussian convergence.  Finite represented-rule boundaries are Gaussian-null, so the limiting risk is that of the corresponding Gaussian screened selector and is bounded by (86), contradicting the violation.  Thus primitive regret is uniformly bounded by \(U^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}\).

This transfer ranges over retained \(S\subseteq A\).  Taking \(A=\mathcal K\) and using (92) gives global Bernoulli adaptation; exact-count global adaptation also requires all shares in a compact interior.  At a vanishing action-relevant share, only \(+\infty\) is asserted.  Finally, for stage \(j\), use tolerance \(1/j\), choose \(\lambda_j,T_j,\eta_j\) as above, and choose \(C_j\) so all pilot, split-CLT, snapping, and screening errors are at most \(1/j\), with each subsample divergent and pilot fraction at most \(1/j\).  This diagonal schedule combines (86) with the primitive transfer and Step 2, proving the certified noncompact value, design, and implementation.
statements.justification: The independent screen--decision split converts every unbounded configuration into one of finitely many certified compact subset games and supplies a terminating risk-and-design certificate.
statements.gap: The prior radial construction failed at lower-dimensional near ties; subset screening and the subface lower bound close exactly that gap.
statements.consumer: A prospective saturation experiment can certify the Bernoulli-label or exact-count allocation over the full simplex and deploy the corresponding calibrated selector with uniform partial-tie protection.

statements.statement: For every finite \(A\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and every positive \(v_A,r_A\), the all-selector Gaussian value \(G_A(v_A,r_A)\) equals the infimum over location-invariant selectors \(\delta(x+c\mathbf 1_A)=\delta(x)\).  Every such selector factors measurably through \(D_Ax\), and the quotient observation has law \(N(D_Ah,\Omega_A)\).  The same equivalence holds for \(G_{A,M}\).  Moreover \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\) as \(M\to\infty\).
statements.justification: This removes the spurious information created by observing a centered representative while retaining the common-location nuisance.
statements.gap: The reduction is specialized here to the exact quotient and compact games used by the mechanism theorem.
statements.consumer: It is used by both LAN lower experiments, the two-policy solution, and the compact certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(d=|A|\), \(\mathbf1=\mathbf1_A\), and \(L(h,a)=\max_kh_k-h_a\).  Then \(L(h+c\mathbf1,a)=L(h,a)\).  For a randomized selector \(\delta=(\delta_a)_a\), define its F{\o}lner average
\[
 \delta_{a,T}(x)=\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^T\delta_a(x+c\mathbf1)\,dc.
\]
Gaussian translation and loss invariance imply
\[
 R(h,\delta_T)=\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^TR(h+c\mathbf1,\delta)\,dc
 \leq\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^A}R(u,\delta). \tag{27}
\]
The functions \(\delta_{a,T}\) lie in the unit ball of \(L^2\) on each bounded box.  To obtain a limit without adding a compactness hypothesis, fix a countable orthonormal basis on each box.  Every coefficient sequence is bounded; successive Bolzano--Weierstrass subsequences, diagonalized over bases, boxes, and the finite actions, make every coefficient converge.  The sums of squared limiting coefficients are at most one because this holds for every finite partial sum, so the limits define \(L^2\) functions and convergence is weak by approximation with finite basis spans.  A further diagonal subsequence gives limits \(\bar\delta_a\) on all boxes; testing against negative parts and against \(\sum_a\bar\delta_a-1\) preserves nonnegativity and \(\sum_a\bar\delta_a=1\).  Against a fixed Gaussian density times the bounded-on-compact loss, weak convergence passes the integral on each box, while Gaussian tails control its complement.  Hence (27) gives \(R(h,\bar\delta)\leq\sup_uR(u,\delta)\) for every fixed \(h\), and therefore the same inequality after taking \(\sup_h\).

For fixed \(c_0\), the two intervals in the averages defining \(\delta_T(x+c_0\mathbf1)\) and \(\delta_T(x)\) differ in total length at most \(2|c_0|\), so their difference is bounded by \(|c_0|/T\).  Passing first for rational \(c_0\) and then using continuity of translations in local \(L^2\) yields a version satisfying \(\bar\delta(x+c\mathbf1)=\bar\delta(x)\) for every real \(c\).  Thus invariant selectors attain the same infimum; the reverse inequality follows because they form a subclass.

The matrix \(D_A\) has rank \(d-1\), kernel \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), and right inverse \(J_A=D_A'(D_AD_A')^{-1}\).  An invariant measurable selector is constant on every fiber of \(D_A\), hence factors measurably through \(D_Ax\).  Linear Gaussian transformation gives
\[
 D_AX\sim N(D_Ah,D_A\Sigma D_A')=N(D_Ah,\Omega_A).
\]
For nonzero \(u\), \(D_A'u\ne0\) and
\[
 u'\Omega_Au=(D_A'u)'\Sigma(D_A'u)>0, \tag{28}
\]
so the quotient covariance is positive definite.  The same argument applies on a fixed quotient ball.

Finally, invariant risks depend only on \(g=D_Ah\), and the balls \(\{g:\|g\|_2\leq M\}\) increase to \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\).  Thus \(G_{A,M}\) is nondecreasing and at most \(G_A\).  Choose \(1/M\)-optimal selectors on successive balls and repeat the diagonal weak-compactness argument on quotient-observation boxes.  The limit has risk at most \(\lim_MG_{A,M}\) at every fixed \(g\), hence on the union of the balls.  Therefore \(G_A\leq\lim_MG_{A,M}\), proving \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\).

statements.statement:
For positive \(v_A,r_A\), \(s>0\), and \(r'_A\geq r_A\) coordinatewise,
\[
G_A(v_A,sr_A)=s^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A),\qquad G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
If \((1-\xi)r_A\leq r'_A\leq(1+\xi)r_A\) with \(0<\xi<1\), then
\[
(1+\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq(1-\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
The positive-rate value is finite and strictly positive.  Under the lower-semicontinuous boundary definition, if any action-relevant coordinate \(r_i\) is zero, then \(G_A(v_A,r_A)=+\infty\).
statements.justification: This supplies the scale, comparison, continuity, and boundary facts required to optimize on closed design simplices.
statements.gap: The zero-rate conclusion is proved from an action-relevant two-arm subexperiment rather than imposed by convention.
statements.consumer: It certifies optimizer existence and the exact-hit mass lower bound.
statements.proof_tex:
For homogeneity, write \(X=h+\operatorname{diag}(v_k/(sr_k))^{1/2}Z\), set \(\widetilde X=\sqrt sX\) and \(\widetilde h=\sqrt sh\), and use the bijection \(\widetilde\delta(\widetilde x)=\delta(\widetilde x/\sqrt s)\).  The transformed experiment has rates \(r_A\), whereas its regret is \(\sqrt s\) times the original regret.  Taking infima and suprema proves
\[
 G_A(v_A,sr_A)=s^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A). \tag{29}
\]
If \(r'_k\geq r_k>0\), add independent coordinatewise Gaussian noise of variance \(v_k/r_k-v_k/r'_k\) to the rate-\(r'_A\) observation.  The resulting law is the rate-\(r_A\) experiment.  Composition with this parameter-free kernel proves
\[
G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A). \tag{30}
\]
Applying (29)--(30) to \((1-\xi)r_A\leq r'_A\leq(1+\xi)r_A\) proves the stated two-sided modulus.

Finiteness follows from the largest-coordinate rule.  If \(i\) is best and \(d_j=h_i-h_j\), then
\[
R(h,\delta_{\max})\leq\sum_{j\ne i}d_j
 \Phi\!\left(-\frac{d_j}{\sqrt{v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j}}\right)
\leq\kappa\sum_{j\ne i}\sqrt{v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j}<\infty. \tag{31}
\]
For positivity, restrict to two arms \(i\ne j\), send all other means to \(-H\), and place equal prior mass on two quotient points having gap \(d\) with opposite signs.  In the quotient experiment, the sign test has error \(\Phi(-d/a_{ij})\), where \(a_{ij}^2=v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j\), and Bayes regret \(d\Phi(-d/a_{ij})\).  Letting \(H\to\infty\) and maximizing at \(d=a_{ij}x\) gives
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)\geq\kappa a_{ij}>0. \tag{32}
\]
If an action-relevant \(r_i^{(m)}\downarrow0\), choose any other action-relevant \(j\); the right side of (32) diverges.  Thus every positive sequence approaching such a boundary has limit inferior \(+\infty\), and the stipulated lower-semicontinuous boundary value is \(+\infty\).

statements.statement:
Let \(A\) be finite with \(d=|A|\geq2\), let \(v_i,r_i>0\), and write
\[
\Sigma=\Sigma(v_A,r_A)=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i^2:i\in A),
\qquad \sigma_i^2=v_i/r_i,
\qquad \bar\sigma=\max_{i\in A}\sigma_i.
\]
For every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\), let \(G_{S,M}(v_S,r_S)\) denote the compact quotient game obtained by restricting the Gaussian face-game definition to \(S\), with the singleton value set equal to zero.  Fix \(0<\lambda<1\), \(T>0\), and for every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\) choose \(M_S\) satisfying
\[
M_S\geq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,T\sqrt{|S|-1},
\qquad
H_{\lambda,T}(v_A,r_A)=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq A}G_{S,M_S}(v_S,r_S),
\qquad
a_\lambda=\sqrt{2/\lambda}\,\bar\sigma.
\]
If, for each \(S\), a represented invariant selector has risk at most \(G_{S,M_S}(v_S,r_S)+\eta\) on its displayed compact quotient ball, then an explicit randomized invariant selector in the unbounded \(A\)-arm experiment satisfies
\[
H_{\lambda,T}(v_A,r_A)
\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)
\leq \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{i\in A}h_i-h_{\delta(X)}\right]
\leq
(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\{H_{\lambda,T}(v_A,r_A)+\eta\}
+\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{T^2}{2a_\lambda^2}\right\}.
\]
The construction and bound hold uniformly on every compact cell of positive diagonal variances and simultaneously over the finitely many retained subsets \(S\subseteq A\).  This is adaptation within the declared face \(A\); adaptation over every candidate policy requires applying the construction with \(A=\mathcal K\) and positive information for every candidate.  In particular, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\),
\[
G_S(v_S,r_S)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
For a selector \(\delta\), write
\[
R_A(\delta,h)=\mathbb E_h[\max_{i\in A}h_i-h_{\delta(X)}]. \tag{56}
\]
Fix nonempty \(S\subseteq A\) and \(M<\infty\).  Every class in the compact \(S\)-game has a representative \(g\) with \(\max_{i\in S}g_i=0\); \(\lVert[g]\rVert_S\leq M\) implies \(-2M\leq g_i\leq0\).  Embed it by
\[
h_i=g_i\ (i\in S),\qquad h_j=-2M-1\ (j\notin S). \tag{57}
\]
Outside actions are dominated.  Diagonal covariance makes \(X_{A\setminus S}\) independent of \(X_S\), with a law independent of \(g\), so those coordinates provide only randomization already allowed to \(S\)-selectors.  Replacing an outside action by a fixed action in \(S\) cannot increase regret.  Hence
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)\geq G_{S,M}(v_S,r_S). \tag{58}
\]
Letting \(M\to\infty\) and using \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\) proves \(G_S\leq G_A\), and maximizing (58) at the displayed radii proves \(H_{\lambda,T}\leq G_A\).

Write \(X=h+\xi\), independently generate \(E\sim N(0,\Sigma)\), and put
\[
X^{\mathrm s}=X+\sqrt{(1-\lambda)/\lambda}\,E,\qquad
X^{\mathrm d}=X-\sqrt{\lambda/(1-\lambda)}\,E. \tag{59}
\]
Then
\[
X^{\mathrm s}\sim N(h,\Sigma/\lambda),\qquad
X^{\mathrm d}\sim N(h,\Sigma/(1-\lambda)),\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(X^{\mathrm s},X^{\mathrm d})=0. \tag{60}
\]
Joint Gaussianity makes the two observations independent.  Retain
\[
\widehat S=\{i:X_i^{\mathrm s}\geq\max_jX_j^{\mathrm s}-T\}. \tag{61}
\]
Conditional on \(\widehat S=S\), feed \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,X_S^{\mathrm d}\) to the compact selector.  Its covariance is \(\Sigma_{SS}\), its mean is \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}h_S\), and the construction is measurable and location invariant.

Let \(b\) maximize \(h\), set \(d_i=h_b-h_i\), and write \(\xi^{\mathrm s}=X^{\mathrm s}-h\).  Each screening contrast has standard deviation at most \(a_\lambda=\sqrt{2/\lambda}\bar\sigma\).  Since
\[
\Phi(-x)\leq\varphi(x)/x\qquad(x>0), \tag{62}
\]
if \(b\notin\widehat S\), summing over a maximizing screening coordinate gives deletion loss at most
\[
\frac{(d-1)a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}. \tag{63}
\]
If retained \(i,j\) have true gap \(D>2T\), then the opposite screening-noise contrast is at least \(D-T\geq D/2\); (62) gives
\[
D\Pr\{i,j\text{ retained}\}
\leq\frac{2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}. \tag{64}
\]
The range of a bad retained set is bounded by the sum of its oriented pairwise gaps.  Summing (63)--(64) over fewer than \(d^2\) indices is at most the displayed tail term.

Otherwise the true range in \(S=\widehat S\) is at most \(2T\), and therefore
\[
\lVert[\sqrt{1-\lambda}h_S]\rVert_S
\leq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}T\sqrt{|S|-1}\leq M_S. \tag{65}
\]
Independence means conditioning on the screen does not alter the decision law.  The scaled conditional regret is at most \(G_{S,M_S}+\eta\); undoing the scale multiplies it by \((1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\).  Averaging over the partition by retained subsets costs their maximum, not their sum.  Combining (58), (63)--(65) proves the bound.  The constants are uniform on compact positive-variance cells and over the finite subsets \(S\subseteq A\).  No arm outside the declared \(A\) enters; global adaptation therefore requires \(A=\mathcal K\) and positive information for each candidate.

statements.statement: For a locally asymptotically normal sequence of dominated experiments with Gaussian-shift limit, every finite-prior Bayes risk of the limit experiment is a lower bound on the limit inferior of the corresponding local maximal risks for measurable randomized decision rules, whenever the losses on the finite local parameter set are bounded and converge to the limit loss.

statements.statement:
Let \(C_B,C_{CR}>0\) be cluster budgets for the optimized Bernoulli-label and exact-count designs.  If the Bernoulli design is required to have no larger leading local simple regret than the exact-count design, namely
\[
\frac{R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)}{\sqrt{C_B}}
\leq
\frac{R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)}{\sqrt{C_{CR}}},
\]
then
\[
\frac{C_B}{C_{CR}}
\geq
\left\{\frac{R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)}{R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)}\right\}^{2}
\geq\frac1{s_{A,\max}}
\geq\frac1{1-2^{1-n}}.
\]
Equality in the mechanism inequality \(\{R_{B,A}^\star/R_{CR,A}^\star\}^2\geq1/s_{A,\max}\) holds exactly under the support-and-normalized-active-vector criterion in \(\texttt{thm:mechanism-loss}\).
statements.justification: The squared local-regret ratio is the operational cluster-count penalty.
statements.gap: The mechanism theorem's risk frontier needs an explicit prospective sample-size implication.
statements.consumer: A designer can translate exact-hit mass loss into a lower bound on required Bernoulli-label clusters.
statements.proof_tex:
All mechanism values are positive by \(\texttt{thm:mechanism-loss}\).  Squaring the assumed leading-regret comparison and rearranging gives
\[
\frac{C_B}{C_{CR}}\geq
\left\{\frac{R_{B,A}^\star}{R_{CR,A}^\star}\right\}^{2}. \tag{46}
\]
Squaring the mechanism bound gives the next inequality and preserves its equality criterion.  Convexity of \(x\mapsto x^n\) gives, for \(x\in[0,1]\),
\[
x^n+(1-x)^n\geq2(1/2)^n=2^{1-n}. \tag{47}
\]
Every active target count is strictly between zero and \(n\), so for column \(\ell\),
\[
\sum_{k\in A}B_{k\ell}
\leq1-\pi_\ell^n-(1-\pi_\ell)^n\leq1-2^{1-n}. \tag{48}
\]
Maximizing over \(\ell\) gives \(s_{A,\max}\leq1-2^{1-n}\).  Reciprocation is valid because the quantities are positive, and (46)--(48) prove the result.

sampling_model.design: Exactly one regime is active. In \(\mathsf B(p)\), labels are iid categorical and units are conditionally independent Bernoulli. In \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the label vector has fixed counts \(C_{C,k}\) and each cluster is conditionally uniform on its exact-count slice.
sampling_model.units: Observe \(C\) independent equal-size cluster schedules from an unrestricted binary potential-outcome law, with no interference across clusters and arbitrary interference within a cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The schedule law \(P\) is mapped to observed data by the known kernel \(R_{B,p}\) or the joint fixed-count kernel \(R^{CR}_{C_C}\); scores and influence functions live in the induced observed-law spaces.
sampling_model.overlap: Interior rational saturations make every Bernoulli hit rate positive. Active-face CR results require positive shares only on \(A\); the full-vector CR CLT and all-policy rank theorem require \(\alpha_k>0\) for every reported policy.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate assignment-specific means and variances within realized target cells, average cells uniformly within each exact-count slice, and use a prespecified bounded fallback for empty cells. Covariance-driven selection may use sample splitting.

estimand_functional: \(\widetilde U_C=(M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z)_{k\in\mathcal K}\), with full covariance \(\Sigma_B^{(K)}\) under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}\) under all-positive-share \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\).

tldr: The headline result prices the loss from implementing exact-count policy ranking through Bernoulli labels: after projecting to any tied-best face, the optimized regret ratio is bounded by the active exact-hit mass and has an exact equality frontier. Separate observed-law theorems establish finite-sample nuisance deletion, full-menu calibrated CLTs, active-face LAN lower experiments, and tie-valid rank inference. The closest same-target estimator is transcribed exactly from Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1); its derived influence variance reveals cross-label, assignment-cell, and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses. A non-symmetric three-policy menu with unequal variances supplies certified optimizer boxes, attained Gaussian risks, and calibrated oracle-to-data transfer. Uniform certification across changing faces and covariance boundaries remains open.

project_justification.gap: Same-target saturation-ranking work uses the nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson estimator in Appendix-B Eq. (S1) and a rule-specific regret envelope; it does not give all-rule nuisance deletion, observed-law target tangents, or a face-specific optimized mechanism-deficiency frontier.
project_justification.niche: Exact-count deployment exposes a known hit polytope \(B\Delta_K\) inside an unrestricted interference model, allowing the assignment mechanism itself to be priced for the same causal target while keeping schedule and observed-data laws distinct.
project_justification.fill: The project makes mechanism loss the sole headline, derives its observed-score and efficiency foundations, proves the exact Han variance comparison, and couples a Joo-informed static Gaussian selector to calibrated cluster data and a certified asymmetric outer design.

technical_internal_limitation: Raw hit pooling is not universally efficient when assignment-specific means vary inside an exact-count slice. The four count-one assignment means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\) yield \(\rho_1^2=1/4\) and \(\tau_1^2=4/25\). Han--Owusu--Shin Eq. (S1) additionally pays the first-stage Horvitz--Thompson participation term \(U_k^2(1/\eta_k-1)\). The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) target-bit witness instead has \(\tau_k^2=1/4\) and information \(4q_k\); it is a special lower-bound witness, not the general exponential-tilt score construction.
honest_scope: The results concern fixed \(n\), fixed \(K\), equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations, isolated iid cluster schedules, and exact-slice welfare. Bernoulli-label and exact-count complete randomization are mutually exclusive regimes, and all scores are defined under their induced observed laws. Active-face CR results allow zero inactive shares, but the full-menu CR CLT and rank theorem require every reported share to be positive. At a unique best policy first-order local regret is zero. When \(K=2\), the face game reduces to the classical sign rule and Neyman allocation; assignment-homogeneous slice means eliminate the calibration component but not necessarily the Horvitz--Thompson participation term in Eq. (S1). The finite positive-face Gaussian certificate and asymmetric three-policy design are theorem targets. A single certificate uniform across data-dependent face changes, covariance perturbations, and admissible boundary limits remains open. The Kenya design is a prospective design consumer rather than an authorized reanalysis.
